content.user_title: Review Code Across Five Quality Axes
content.value_statement: Code reviews often miss risks when they focus only on tests or style. This skill guides a consistent review of correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews changes for correctness, edge cases, error paths, and test coverage.
Checks readability, complexity, naming, duplication, and dead code.
Assesses architecture, module boundaries, abstractions, and dependency changes.
Reviews common security risks, including input validation, secrets, injection, and authorization.
Checks performance risks such as unbounded work, N+1 queries, and missing pagination.
Produces prioritized findings with suggested structural remedies and verification checks.
limitations: It cannot run tests, builds, profilers, or dependency audits by itself.
It cannot confirm runtime behavior without accurate context and verification evidence.
It provides review guidance, not a replacement for security specialists or maintainers.
It does not inspect files that are not supplied in the review context.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Evaluate a proposed change before merge with prioritized findings across correctness, design, security, and performance.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers and pull request reviewers

use_cases.title: Validate AI-Generated Code
use_cases.description: Inspect code produced by an agent for hidden assumptions, weak tests, unsafe patterns, and unnecessary complexity.

use_cases.title: Plan a Safer Refactor
use_cases.description: Separate structural improvements from feature work and identify simpler designs before implementation begins.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Change Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance. List the most important issues first.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured first review.

prompt_templates.title: Test Coverage Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change and its tests. Identify missing edge cases, weak assertions, error paths, and regressions the tests would not catch.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer wants to validate a test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this change for coupling, duplication, misplaced responsibilities, abstraction debt, and complexity that was relocated rather than removed.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release-readiness review. Prioritize correctness and security risks, inspect dependency changes, assess verification evidence, and propose concrete remedies.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced reviewer is preparing a high-impact change for merge.

output_examples.input: Review a feature change that adds a list endpoint and updates its tests.
output: Required: Add pagination before accepting unbounded result sets.
Required: Add an error-path test for a failed data request.
Consider: Move filtering logic into the module that owns the query.

output_examples.input: Review a dependency upgrade that changes the lockfile.
output_examples.output: Review the changelog and lockfile diff, isolate the package change, run the full test suite, and verify that transitive updates are expected.

output_examples.input: Review an AI-generated refactor with passing tests.
output: The tests pass, but the refactor preserves the same branching complexity.
Move feature-specific logic out of the shared module.
Add regression coverage for the changed boundary.

best_practices: Understand the change intent and tests before inspecting implementation details.
Lead with high-impact correctness and security findings, then discuss structure and style.
Pair each structural concern with a concrete remedy and verification step.
anti_patterns: Approving a change because its tests pass while ignoring security or architecture.
Reporting a long list of cosmetic nits before one serious correctness issue.
Combining broad refactoring, feature work, and dependency upgrades without isolation.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.

faq.question: Can it review code from an AI assistant?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to examine code from humans, agents, and mixed teams.

faq.question: Does it run tests or builds?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates supplied verification evidence and identifies missing checks.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Correctness and security come first, followed by structural risks, simplifications, and minor style concerns.

faq.question: Can it review dependency upgrades?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks changelog review, package isolation, lockfile changes, vulnerabilities, and test evidence.

faq.question: Is it a replacement for security review?
faq.answer: No. It provides practical review guidance, but sensitive changes still need qualified security review.
